Breslau
bres'low
n. (the capital of Silesia on the Oder, now Wroclaw; a Lutheran city under a Catholic bishop for three centuries)
From the Slavic personal name Vratislav, germanised Breslau; the Polish Wroclaw preserves the older form.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

Breslau was the chief city of Silesia and the seat of its bishop. The council called Johann Hess to St Mary Magdalene in 1523, held a public disputation in 1524, and carried the city over to the Reformation within a few years, while the bishop and his cathedral chapter remained Catholic and stayed where they were. The result was one of the longest-running arrangements of its kind in Europe: a Lutheran city with Lutheran parish churches, a Lutheran school and a Lutheran press, governing itself around a Catholic cathedral precinct it could not touch, under Habsburg sovereigns who were the leading Catholic power on the continent. It lasted, with pressure and interruption, until Prussia took Silesia in 1741. The dictionary records the city because the word made its way there by preaching in a town the gospel did not politically control: “So mightily grew the word of God and prevailed” (Act 19:20).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines to prevail as to overcome, to gain the victory or superiority; a chapter as an assembly of the clergy of a cathedral; and a precinct as a district within certain boundaries.

expand to see more

PREVAIL, v.i. [L. praevaleo.] To overcome; to gain the victory or superiority; to be in force; to have effect.

CHAPTER, n. [L. capitulum.] A society of clergymen belonging to a cathedral or collegiate church; the body of canons.

PRECINCT, n. [L. praecinctus.] The limit, bound or exterior line encompassing a place; a district within certain boundaries.

RICHLY, adv. With riches; with abundance; plenteously; truly; abundantly.

ADMONISH, v.t. [L. admoneo.] To warn or notify of a fault; to reprove with mildness; to counsel against wrong practices.

Modern Corruption

The Silesian capital on the Oder, now Wroclaw; Lutheran by council decision in the 1520s while its bishop and cathedral chapter remained Catholic until Prussia annexed Silesia in 1741.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. Breslau is nevertheless a standing rebuke to a view held in every century, that the gospel cannot flourish where it does not hold the levers. The Breslau Lutherans had no sovereign of their own confession, a Catholic bishop inside their walls, and a Habsburg emperor over their heads who spent the seventeenth century dismantling Protestantism elsewhere in Silesia. What they had was preaching, a school, a press and a council that would not budge, and with those they kept a Lutheran city for two hundred years.

The principle to recover is that the word grows by its own power, and that its growth is reported as the word's achievement rather than the church's. Luke credits neither strategy nor patronage: “So mightily grew the word of God and prevailed” (Act 19:20). The means is the public hearing of it, with a whole city turning out — “And the next sabbath day came almost the whole city together to hear the word of God” (Act 13:44). And the way it is kept in a place is by lodging it in the people: “Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom” (Col 3:16).

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Greek auxano (G837), to grow or increase; Greek ischuo (G2480), to be strong or prevail.

Greek auxano (G837) — to grow, to increase; “So mightily grew the word of God”, Acts 19:20.

Greek ischuo (G2480) — to be strong, to have power, to prevail; Acts 19:20.

Greek enoikeo (G1774) — to dwell in, to inhabit; “dwell in you richly”, Colossians 3:16.

Greek plousios (G4146) — richly, abundantly; Colossians 3:16.

Greek noutheteo (G3560) — to admonish, to warn, to put in mind; Colossians 3:16.

Usage

"“So mightily grew the word of God and prevailed” (Act 19:20) — Johann Hess called to St Mary Magdalene, 1523."

"“And the next sabbath day came almost the whole city together to hear the word of God” (Act 13:44) — the public disputation of 1524."

"“Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom” (Col 3:16) — a Lutheran city around a Catholic cathedral for two centuries."
